family.description: Iron-sulphur (FeS) clusters are important cofactors for numerous proteins involved in electron transfer, in redox and non-redox catalysis, in gene regulation, and as sensors of oxygen and iron. These functions depend on the various FeS cluster prosthetic groups, the most common being [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] [[cite:PUB00035635]]. FeS cluster assembly is a complex process involving the mobilisation of Fe and S atoms from storage sources, their assembly into [Fe-S] form, their transport to specific cellular locations, and their transfer to recipient apoproteins. So far, three FeS assembly machineries have been identified, which are capable of synthesising all types of [Fe-S] clusters: ISC (iron-sulphur cluster), SUF (sulphur assimilation), and NIF (nitrogen fixation) systems. The SUF system is an alternative pathway to the ISC system that operates under iron starvation and oxidative stress. It is found in eubacteria, archaea and eukaryotes (plastids). The SUF system is encoded by the suf operon (sufABCDSE), and the six encoded proteins are arranged into two complexes (SufSE and SufBCD) and one protein (SufA). SufS is a pyridoxal-phosphate (PLP) protein displaying cysteine desulphurase activity. SufE acts as a scaffold protein that accepts S from SufS and donates it to SufA [[cite:PUB00035639]]. SufC is an ATPase with an unorthodox ATP-binding cassette (ABC)-like component. SufA is homologous to IscA [[cite:PUB00035640]], acting as a scaffold protein in which Fe and S atoms are assembled into [FeS] cluster forms, which can then easily be transferred to apoproteins targets. This entry represents the core domain of SufB and SufD proteins, which are homologous, and form part of the SufBCD complex in the SUF system [[cite:PUB00089444]]. SufB accepts sulfur transferred from SufE [[cite:PUB00089442]], whereas SufD may play a role in iron acquisition [[cite:PUB00089443]].

causal_graphs.context: Compare each variant with its panel's WT at 3 uM SufBCD, with 0.5 uM SufS, 2 uM SufE, 2 mM L-cysteine and 2 mM DTT in 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 150 mM NaCl, 30 C for 10 min. Released sulfide is detected as methylene blue and activity normalized per mg SufS. pGSO164-derived complexes were expressed in YT2512 and chromatographically purified; SufS and untagged SufE were separately supplied.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4a and Methods establish the WT comparison, nonzero baseline and complete reaction; supplemental S3 and Figure 4b qualify assembly and interaction alternatives.
Reference sequence and locally translated mutation primers establish the family mapping, not the experiment's inferred sulfur trajectory.

edges.mechanism: C254A-containing complex yields less sulfide output than WT and remains near the no-added-complex baseline. The directly observed substitution effect concerns the assembled reaction, not isolated-domain catalysis or absolute loss of all cysteine desulfuration.
edges.subject: sufb-c254a-complex

evidence.explanation: The separate Q285A panel in visually inspected Figure 4a supports the partial decrease relative to WT retained here, not total loss of stimulation.

edges.mechanism: The Q285A preparation yields lower activity than its matched WT at 3 uM complex while remaining above the no-complex baseline. Partial stimulation is retained, without assigning an atomic contact or independently observed sulfur-transfer microstep.
edges.subject: sufb-q285a-complex

evidence.explanation: Figure 4a's W287A panel and its stated reaction conditions support this bounded decrease relative to WT, with residual stimulation preserved.

edges.mechanism: W287A lowers the sulfide-output activity relative to its matched WT at 3 uM complex, but does not eliminate stimulation. This purified-system comparison is not a direct binding-affinity or tunnel-gating measurement.
edges.subject: sufb-w287a-complex

causal_graphs.family_mapping: E. coli K12 SufB is UniProtKB:P77522, 495 aa, sequence version 2, with PF01458 at 225-466. C254, Q285 and W287 lie inside it. Partner SufD P77689 has the homologous family interval 166-393 but does not inherit the SufB-specific substitution effect. Table S2 C254A primers agree locally with the reference; full historical clones and junctions remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: C254A removes added-complex stimulation, not basal SufSE output. Q285A/W287A retain stimulation. This net purified-system readout does not directly track persulfide chemistry or assign the chemical step responsible. S3 supports comparable complex assembly and Figure 4b retains SufE interaction, but neither proves identical local folding. Means and SD reflect at least three measurements, not established independent protein batches.

causal_graphs.scope: Purified E. coli SufBCD complexes carrying separate C254A, Q285A or W287A SufB substitutions in Yuda 2017 Figure 4a; not isolated PF01458 or a stand-alone SufB desulfurase.
causal_graphs.title: SufB substitutions reduce stimulation of the SufSE sulfide-output assay

causal_graphs.context: React 10 uM SufBCD, 0.5 uM each SufS/SufE and 2 mM L-cysteine in 125 ul of 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 150 mM NaCl at 30 C for 3 h without DTT. Remove smaller components using a 100-kDa ultrafilter, normalize retained complex by A280, then release bound sulfur with 2 mM DTT and measure methylene blue at 670 nm. Means/SD derive from at least three measurements.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4c and the separate no-DTT loading/separation protocol support the complex-level sulfur decrease. The authors' transfer interpretation is not promoted to a directly tracked atomic trajectory.

edges.mechanism: Replacing SufB C254 with alanine reduces the complex-associated sulfur signal to below detection in the loading/separation assay. This directly tests the variant preparation but does not itself observe individual trans-persulfuration events.
edges.subject: c254a-in-sulfur-loading

evidence.explanation: Figure 4c and its Results provide the residual sulfur comparison for C405A; Figure 4a separately shows preserved stimulation, preventing conflation of the endpoints.

edges.mechanism: C405A reduces retained sulfur relative to WT while leaving measurable residual sulfur. Its approximately WT Figure 4a stimulation remains a distinct negative control against treating every readout as the same causal step.
edges.subject: c405a-in-sulfur-loading

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P77522 SufB has PF01458 225-466, encompassing both C254 and C405. C254A and C405A primer pairs encode only their intended local substitutions relative to the current sequence. Intact SufBCD and required SufS/SufE partners were assayed, not the isolated family region.
causal_graphs.limitations: WT retains 4.8 +/- 0.9 sulfur atoms per complex, C405A 1.0 +/- 0.1, and C254A has no detected signal; the detection limit is unspecified. Retained sulfur is an operational complex-level endpoint, not proof of every attachment site, a C254-to-C405 transfer trajectory, FADH2 chemistry or an assembled Fe-S cluster. SufD C358A retains roughly WT sulfur and is not represented as another loss mutation.

causal_graphs.context: UT109 carries pUMV22 Sp-r, pRK-sufABC-SE and pBBR-sufD encoding WT or H360A. Compare LB plate growth without MVA at 37 C for 24 h; the figure also includes vector and other SufD substitutions. Glucose supplementation of this particular plate is not independently specified beyond the general supplemented-medium method.

evidence.explanation: Supplemental Figure S2a and Table S1 establish the phenotype and strain; the main-text abundance qualification and S2c prevent an equal-expression or direct-ligation claim.
Locates H360 in the homologous SufD core without transferring SufB-specific sulfur effects to it.

edges.mechanism: H360A does not support the WT-complemented growth phenotype in the visually inspected S2a plates. The cellular effect remains indirect because Fe-S assembly, expression and downstream metabolism are not resolved into a measured molecular chain.
edges.subject: h360a-complementing-allele

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Reference P77689 SufD, 423 aa, sequence version 1, maps PF01458 to 166-393 and H360 falls within that region. UT109 is explicitly an MG1655 derivative in Table S1. The allele is expressed as an intact protein, not an isolated domain or the homologous SufB protein.
causal_graphs.limitations: This is failed complementation under a specific bypass-dependent condition, not unconditional lethality or observed iron ligation. SufD H360A abundance is somewhat lower in the separately supplemented liquid-culture Western experiment; altered abundance can contribute. MVA-supported viability and WT complementation do not establish a residue-specific chemical mechanism.

causal_graphs.context: UT109 with pUMV22 Sp-r, pRK-sufABC-SE and WT or H360A pBBR-sufD is grown in Superbroth with glucose and MVA at 37 C to early stationary phase. General supplementation is 0.4% glucose and 200 uM racemic mevalonolactone. Cell-density-normalized lysates undergo native PAGE and anti-Fdx Western blotting; Suf protein abundance is assessed separately by SDS-PAGE/Western blotting.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected S2b/c, Figure 1's referenced assay caption and Methods support the endpoint and abundance qualification. This culture contains MVA absent from the separate plate comparison; exact plate glucose is unresolved.

edges.mechanism: S2b shows less detected holo-Fdx with H360A than with WT SufD under the supplemented liquid-culture conditions. The result is retained as an indirect cellular maturation-associated phenotype, not direct proof of a particular Fe-S ligand or transfer route.
edges.subject: h360a-supplemented-culture

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P77689 SufD contains PF01458 at 166-393, including H360. This is a whole-protein substitution in an MG1655-derived host; the family also contains SufB but its reactions are not equivalent experimental evidence.
causal_graphs.limitations: Holo-Fdx signal is not a direct measurement of all cellular Fe-S clusters or a purified insertion reaction. Apo-Fdx is not detected, so total Fdx stability is an alternative contribution. SufD H360A is somewhat less abundant; the Western control does not establish equal expression. No quantified fold-change, replicate confidence or serial connection to the plate-growth graph is claimed.
